concept.name: Order block
concept.definition: In SMC/ICT vocabulary, the last opposite-direction candle (or consecutive cluster of them) before an impulsive move — the final down candle before a rally (bullish) or the final up candle before a decline (bearish) — marked as a zone that may be defended on a return. It is read as the footprint of institutional position-building; that reading is an interpretation, since the candle alone shows only price, not orders.
concept.intuition: The last place price sat before the big move launched is treated as the move's origin — and origins are where defenders may remain.
concept.mechanics: Find the displacement first (an impulsive leg that breaks structure or sweeps a swing, ideally leaving a fair value gap), then step back to the last opposite close and box its range — conventions include full high-low, body only, or the 50% mean threshold. A decisive close through the whole zone invalidates it; the failed zone is then watched as a 'breaker' from the other side.
concept.failure_modes: Candidate blocks are everywhere, so most are meaningless; price trades straight through a large share of them, and there is no reliable published hit rate for the concept.
concept.misconceptions: That an order block visibly shows institutional orders; only the candle is observable, and the institutional-footprint narrative cannot be verified from the chart.
concept.example: A pair sweeps a low, then rallies impulsively through the prior swing high; the last down-close candle before that leg is boxed as a bullish order block, watched for longs on the retrace (mitigation).
